Destinations / Ladakh

Ladakh

High passes, turquoise lakes and monasteries on the roof of the world

Best time: June – September. Stunning but high altitude (3,500 m+). Plan 2 acclimatisation days in Leh; best for kids 8+.

Highlights

  • Pangong Tso at sunrise
  • Khardung La, one of the highest motorable passes
  • Star-gazing in Hanle dark-sky reserve
  • Nubra Valley sand dunes and Bactrian camels

Suggested road trips

Manali → Leh Highway

5 days · about 480 km. Classic high-altitude drive through the Atal Tunnel and over Baralacha La and Tanglang La with camps at Jispa and Sarchu.

  1. Manali → Jispa (140 km, about 5 h): Through the Atal Tunnel, which skips the Rohtang climb.
  2. Jispa → Sarchu (90 km, about 4 h): Over Baralacha La (about 4,890 m). Sleep lower at Jispa another night if anyone feels unwell.
  3. Sarchu → Leh (250 km, about 9 h): Longest day, over Tanglang La (5,300 m+). Start at dawn; no fuel until Karu.
  4. Leh: Rest day to acclimatise. Walk the old town slowly; drink water.
  5. Leh → Shey, Thiksey & Hemis (90 km, about 3 h): Monasteries of the Indus valley, back to Leh.

Leh → Nubra → Pangong loop

4 days · about 460 km. Cross Khardung La to Hunder dunes, then the Shyok river road to Pangong Tso.

  1. Leh → Hunder (Nubra) (125 km, about 5 h): Over Khardung La. Don’t linger at the top.
  2. Hunder → Turtuk and back (170 km, about 5 h): Balti village near the border; the road follows the Shyok river.
  3. Hunder → Pangong Tso (160 km, about 6 h): Shyok road, rough in places. Nights are freezing — a heater helps.
  4. Pangong Tso → Leh (160 km, about 5 h): Over Chang La.

Before you go

Leh is at about 3,500 m. Spend your first 36–48 hours in Leh taking it easy before crossing the high passes — Khardung La and Chang La are above 5,300 m. Acute mountain sickness shows as headache, nausea or breathlessness at rest: stop climbing, and go lower if it gets worse.

On the Manali–Leh highway there is no fuel between Tandi (near Keylong) and Karu — roughly 365 km. Fill up in Leh and Diskit; there is no pump at Pangong. Carry a spare can.

Mostly paved with broken sections, afternoon water crossings on the Manali–Leh road, and snow on the passes early and late in the season. The highways usually open from about June to October.
